items.title: The iPhone 18 Pro Will Probably Cost At Least $1,399
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
The iPhone 18 Pro is just a little over a month away, likely debuting sometime in September, but if you were planning on upgrading, you should probably get ready for a higher price tag.

Apple has already raised prices on most of its Mac and iPad lineup back in June, due to increased memory prices, but the iPhone and Apple Watch were largely unaffected. However, the price increases seem like they're coming stapled onto the new iPhones. According to a research note spotted by 9to5mac, tech analyst Jeff Pu predicts that the iPhone 18 Pro will start at around $1,399, with the larger iPhone Pro Max starting somewhere between $1,449–$1,499.

To put that into perspective, right now you can get the iPhone 17 Pro starting at $1,099 for the regular size, and $1,199 for the Pro Max. If these rumored prices are to be believed, it'll make for a gen-on-gen price increase of around 24%.

This has been an expensive year for smartphones all around. Just last month, Samsung launched the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, which is essentially just a straight sequel to the non-ultra Galaxy Z Fold 7, which carried a $100 price increase. The company also launched a non-ultra Galaxy Z Fold 8 with a worse camera system and a new shape for $1,899 – which was supposed to be the "more affordable" option.

There have been rumors that this will be the year Apple will release its long-awaited foldable. But, with prices being what they are this year, a foldable iPhone would likely be extremely expensive.

These price increases will probably keep adding up over the next year or so, as the AI-driven memory shortage continues to drive prices up. While it's only now starting to hit phones, gaming hardware has been no stranger to these price increases. The Xbox Series X, for instance, went up to $799 this month, and Valve engineers have warned that RAM prices are only getting worse, after the high prices forced the company to release the Steam Machine at a high price.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

items.title: 14 Years After Its Release, Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 Is One of 2026's Best Selling Games, According to Analysts
items.description: The recent PS4 and PS5 ports of Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 are already some of the best-selling games of the year, according to analysts.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The recent PS4 and PS5 ports of Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 are already some of the best-selling games of the year, according to analysts.

Last month, Activision surprised Call of Duty fans by dropping ports of Black Ops 1 and 2 on modern PlayStation consoles. Activision has somewhat notoriously avoided re-releasing older Call of Duty games, as fans speculate that it would distract players from the newer games that are more lucrative for the publisher. Still, it seems that after Black Ops 7 failed to meet expectations last year, these ports were put into production to earn back player trust (and generate some quick cash, too).

That plan worked absurdly well, as Alinea Analytics estimates that Black Ops 2 sold a whopping 8.2 million on PS4 and PS5 last month, while Black Ops 1 sold 3 million. The firm estimated that the games collectively generated $435 million on PlayStation. The two are estimated to be the two highest-selling PlayStation titles of July, with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced trailing in third with 1.6 million copies, roughly half the number of copies sold as a 16-year-old game.

This is a rather astonishing amount and would make Black Ops 2 one of the best-selling games of 2026, period. At the beginning of July, Alinea estimated that the three best-selling games of 2026 were Mecha Chameleon at 12.6 million copies, EA's FC 26 at 9.1 million, and Resident Evil Requiem at 7.5 million. By the end of July, Capcom confirmed Requiem had just surpassed 8 million units sold, so those estimates seem fairly on point. With that said, it looks like Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 is among the top 5 best-selling games of the year so far.

Another notable part of this story is that these ports haven't made any significant changes from their original versions. There are no new features or content, and even the technical aspects largely remain unchanged. It's unclear how much Activision paid developer Iron Galaxy to put these ports together, but they likely didn't spend nearly as much as needed for a remaster or remake. Whether this will open the door to more Call of Duty ports remains to be seen, but vocal fans are hoping to see a return of the original Modern Warfare 2 in the future.

Activision's reign is far from over, though, as Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is set to release this October. While it was released during a very busy season, it will still likely sell gangbusters as the Modern Warfare sub-franchise is the most revered part of Call of Duty.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Pokémon Developer Game Freak Promises Fixes 'Within a Week' To Its Big Budget RPG Beast of Reincarnation, Following Mixed Response at Launch
items.description: Game Freak has promised a series of quick fixes after a mixed response to the launch of its big budget RPG Beast of Reincarnation.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Game Freak has promised a series of quick fixes after a mixed response to the launch of its big budget RPG Beast of Reincarnation.

Best known as the developer of Pokémon, Game Freak has continued to make various other games over the years — though none as ambitious-looking as action role-playing epic Beast of Reincarnation, which launched for PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S yesterday.

But despite some flashy trailers and a lovable-looking dog companion, Beast of Reincarnation has garnered a tepid response from players. On Steam, the game sits with a Mixed user rating after more than 1,600 reviews. IGN's own Beast of Reincarnation review returned a 6/10 score, meanwhile.

"Its execution falls short of its promising ideas," we wrote. "The story is a bland, cliche-filled tale better-told by other games in the genre, combat quickly grows stale due to a lack of enemy variety and the predictable attack patterns that undermine what makes action RPG combat thrive, and boss fights end up being quite disappointing despite looking badass as all get out."

Now, Game Freak has responded to the game's early reception, and promised a list of changes that will arrive in a patch expected to land in the next seven days.

"Thank you for playing Beast of Reincarnation!" Game Freak wrote in a post on social media. "We take your feedback to heart and are currently planning a series of continuous updates." These will include camera adjustments, increased text size, story pacing improvements, bug fixes, and a change to prioritize the game's Performance visual setting rather than its chunkier Cinematic option.

Camera adjustments to move the game's view further back from main character Emma has been a common gripe — so much so that there's already a mod available for PC players to adjust the game's camera and field of view settings. An increase to the game's text size also seems a relatively straightforward and welcome change, though exactly how Game Freak plans to improve the game's story pacing is unclear.

Are you playing Beast of Reincarnation already? What are your thoughts on Game Freak's latest RPG at launch?

items.title: Xbox Console Updates Adding New Capture and Achievement Features
items.description: Xbox has announced another set of new console features, which will begin rolling out to some users from today.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Xbox has announced another set of new console features, which will begin rolling out to some users from today.

As ever, these new features will begin being tested by Xbox Insiders in the Alpha Skip-Ahead ring, before slowing becoming available to all Xbox owners over the coming weeks.

The biggest addition here looks to be the ability to include party chat audio within gameplay captures, so you can fully remember a particular gaming moment and the reactions that came along with it. This feature has been designed so that individual party members can choose whether their audio can be captured, and only will be after players manually opt in.

Achievement hunters will likely celebrate to see an expanded set of options for tracking your progress, with your cheevo list now sortable by Last Played, Completion Percentage, Gamerscore Earned, Number of Achievements Unlocked, and more. And yes, you can sort these categories in ascending or descending order, allowing you to highlight where you're close to the full 1000G, or ready to start unlocking a new game's achievements from the off.

Next up, cloud saves. Players will be able to view and restore previous cloud save versions in supported games, starting with Forza Horizon 6, allowing you to recover an older progress point if necessary. If you ever experience a corrupted save (or want to go back and replay part of a game differently), this option should help you out.

And finally, Xbox is expanding your game wishlist — allowing you to add up to 1,000 titles. That should be enough, surely?

Today's updates come just days after Microsoft's latest set of Xbox console price rises have kicked in, raising the cost of some Xbox Series X and S models by up to $150 in the U.S., and up to an additional £220 in the U.K.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Gaming Made Up Just 6% of AMD's Earnings This Quarter
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
It's no secret that gaming hardware has been getting more expensive this year, so it shouldn't be surprising that people are buying less of it. But, it turns out that AMD's gaming business shrank by a whopping 31% in Q2 2026.

In the second quarter of the year, the gaming business only made $779 million, compared to $1.1 billion in Q2 2025, according to the company's latest earnings report. AMD attributes this loss to "lower semi-custom revenue," which means fewer consoles have been selling over the last few months. This is in a time that would have included the Steam Machine and the AMD Radeon RX 9070 GRE in June 2026.

AMD's gaming revenue is lumped into the Client and Gaming segment, and overall, that portion of the business was up 6% year over year, making $3.8 billion. AMD's processors have been making their way into more modern laptops, especially in the budget range, and while the company's earnings report doesn't lay out exactly which products were selling, it's not hard to imagine that a lot of this growth came at the hands of budget laptops that don't have a ton of RAM.

But while the gaming business isn't doing all that great, AMD is thriving. The company raked in $11.5 billion in revenue last quarter, which is up 51% over this time last year, driven largely by AI. AMD's data center business brought in $6.7 billion last quarter, which is a massive 107% increase over last year. So, even though hardware is more expensive and harder to even obtain, AMD is bringing in more money than ever before.

It's likely that the gaming business will continue to shrink over the next year or so, while AMD cashes in on the AI boom. Especially now that the Xbox Series X officially went up in price and both Team Green and Team Red reportedly plan to raise prices on gaming hardware, it really does seem like gaming hardware is going to continue to fall down the list of AMD and Nvidia's priorities.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

items.title: Diablo 4 Leak Reveals Nintendo Switch 2 Release Date, Price and Code-in-a-Box Physical Release
items.description: Blizzard will launch Diablo 4 on Nintendo Switch 2 next month, a fresh leak has revealed.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Blizzard will launch Diablo 4 on Nintendo Switch 2 next month, a fresh leak has revealed.

As reported by Dealabs' ever-reliable billbil-kun, the Switch 2 version of Diablo 4 will arrive in mid-September priced at $69.99 / £62.99 / €69.99, more than three years after the game first debuted on PC, PlayStation and Xbox back in June 2023.

Alongside a digital launch via the eShop, the game's Switch 2 port will also be released with a physical edition — though this will just contain a digital download code in an otherwise empty box. (Yes, there's not even a Game-Key Card here.)

An exact release date isn't yet available, though it's reported that the game will launch during the third week of September, on either Tuesday 15 or Friday 18. It's also unclear whether the game's Lord of Hatred expansion will also be included.

Today's leak follows months of expectation that Blizzard is prepping an official Switch 2 launch for the game, which has previously popped up on a couple of ratings boards. Exactly when the company will formally announce the port remains to be seen, though we are now just weeks away from the annual Gamescom extravaganza, which once again takes place in Cologne, Germany later this month.

While Diablo 4 may be several years' old at this point, the game still enjoys a dedicated playerbase and received its second big expansion only in April. In May, the game's secret cow level was finally discovered — though after such a long build-up, some players were left a little disappointed.

"Diablo 4 is a stunning sequel with near perfect endgame and progression design that makes it absolutely excruciating to put down," we wrote in IGN's Diablo 4 review, which returned a devilish 9/10 score.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Lee Cronin's The Mummy Movie Poster Banned in U.K. For Depicting 'Realistic Impression of a Dead Child'
items.description: The U.K.'s advertising regulator has slapped Warner Bros. for displaying Lee Cronin's The Mummy movie posters it says are "likely to distress young children."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The U.K.'s advertising regulator has slapped Warner Bros. for displaying Lee Cronin's The Mummy movie posters it says are "likely to distress young children."

Posters for the film had previously been displayed on the London Underground and on billboards across the U.K., prompting 30 complaints to the Advertising Standards Authority (ASA). The matter was highlighted on social media back in April by BBC journalist and broadcaster Samira Ahmed, who said she had personally submitted a complaint to the ASA.

Numerous complaints stated that the poster's imagery was too graphic, and displayed what looked like a dead and mummified child. The image showsed a grey-skinned girl with one eye partially closed, wrapped in ancient bandages. A tagline stated: "Some Things Are Meant to Stay Buried."

Defending the posters, Warner Bros. stated that the girl was actually alive — or, technically, a "living mummy" (which sounds to me more like a class of undead?). Either way, Warner Bros. also argued that the poster showed the girl in a neutral facial expression, and did not depict violence.

The ASA, however, was having none of it. "Because the figure had recognizable human features, we considered that viewers were likely to understand it as a realistic depiction of a dead child," it wrote. "We therefore concluded that the ads were unsuitable for outdoor display and therefore breached the code."

Warner Bros. was also found to have broken a pledge to not place the advert within 100m of a school, as it could be seen directly from a nursery for small children.

Just submitted my complaint to the Advertising Standards Authority about this poster ad at tube stations. Why is there so little consideration of the impact of such images on children? (And one might add, on bereaved parents). pic.twitter.com/gjwca6YDdX

— Samira Ahmed (@SamiraAhmedUK) April 15, 2026

Other complaints about The Mummy's advertising campaign were not upheld, however, including concerns around a TV commercial and similar online version. The ASA found that the advert had been targeted to air after 7.30pm, when young children were less likely to see it. The authority also dismissed additional concerns that the image would be unecessarily distressing to complainants who had lost a child themselves, or who were concerned about the child's depiction in the context of ongoing global conflicts.

Following the ASA's decision, the poster can no longer be displayed publicly in its current form. The authority has also instructed Warner Bros. "to ensure that future marketing that was likely to cause fear or distress to young children did not appear where they were likely to see it."

IGN’s Lee Cronin’s The Mummy Review returned a 7/10. We said: "As ugly as it is amusing, Lee Cronin's The Mummy takes the kind of tonal swings you rarely see from a Hollywood studio."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Secretlab Launches Pokémon-Themed Gaming Chair ‘Skins’ Featuring the Original Three Starter Evolutions
items.author: Bo Moore
items.content:
Secretlab, maker of our favorite gaming chair, the Titan Evo, has launched a new Pokémon-Themed upgrade kit for its chairs. The new looks come in the form of Secretlab Skins, a kind of slip-cover for the Titan Evo line of chairs that let you customize their look without having to buy an entirely new chair.

The new Pokémon Pixel Art Collection features the iconic final evolutions of the original three starter Pokémon: Charizard, Blastoise, and Venusaur, each rendered in a pixel-art style.

These new covers join Secretlab's broader Pokémon collection, which launched earlier this year with chairs (not Skins) featuring Pikachu, Eevee, and Gengar. items.title: Former Pokémon Exec Accused of Hiding Video Cameras in Office Bathroom to Record Women and Girls
items.description: The Pokémon Company's former director of engineering at its Bellevue, Washington headquarters is now the subject of a class-action lawsuit, after the discovery of a hidden camera concealed in one of the building's bathrooms.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The Pokémon Company's former director of engineering at its Bellevue, Washington headquarters is now the subject of a class-action lawsuit, after the discovery of a hidden camera concealed in one of the building's bathrooms.

45-year-old Ben Tsai, the company's former engineering lead, was previously charged with first-degree voyeurism back in January, after the discovery of a video camera in a nearby Starbucks bathroom.

After further investigation, it was alleged that Tsai had also placed cameras in a Safeway store, in his own home, and in the bathroom of his workplace: The Pokémon Company's offices. Tsai was subsequently also charged with dealing and possessing child sexual abuse content, following the alleged discovery of hundreds of videos depicting adult and child nudity, some of which it's claimed he personally recorded.

For his part, Tsai has denied all of the charges.

According to The Seattle Times, Tsai has not been a Pokémon Company employee since the initial charge against him back in January. "Our focus remains on the well-being of our employees," a Pokémon Company spokesperson told the outlet.

However, a fresh class-action lawsuit is seeking to escalate pressure on Tsai, who is still currently being held by cops while on bail. Filed by an unnamed Jane Doe under Washington's anti-discrimination laws, this legal action seeks to represent all women and girls who may have used The Pokémon Company's female bathroom facilities between 2017 and 2026, and alleges that Tsai was likely recording footage not just for his own purposes, but in order to also distribute it further.

"Seeing someone who is engaged in the extensive amount of voyeurism and conduct that he's been charged with, the idea that this was all just for his own personal use and that there was no distribution seems doubtful," said Alex Dietz, an attorney representing Jane Doe.

The lawsuit also takes aim at The Pokémon Company itself, and claims it was negligent of its duty to protect employees by failing to identify Tsai as a potential threat, or control his actions.

Image credit: Behrouz Mehri/AFP via Getty Images

items.title: Beaten Path Revealed for PC and Consoles
items.description: Introducing Beaten Path, a new solo-developed tactical RPG set in a world of ancient machines and fallen gods. The developer (Jarett Gross) cites Fire Emblem and Final Fantasy Tactics as his inspirations. It includes 25 fully voice-acted characters.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Introducing Beaten Path, a new solo-developed tactical RPG set in a world of ancient machines and fallen gods. The developer (Jarett Gross) cites Fire Emblem and Final Fantasy Tactics as his inspirations. It includes 25 fully voice-acted characters. Check out the first trailer above and the first screenshots in the gallery below.

Beaten Path's Kickstarter campaign was fully funded in just six days, and now development progresses. “I started Beaten Path because I wanted to make the kind of tactical RPG I love playing, with meaningful strategy, lots of room for customisation, and a world players can spend time in beyond the battles," Gross said. "It has now been in development for almost five years, and over that time it has grown into something much bigger than I first imagined. The support from the community has meant a lot, and partnering with Wales Interactive is an exciting next step that gives us the chance to bring Beaten Path to more players across PC and consoles. I’m really looking forward to sharing more as development continues.”

Grid-based maps form the foundation of the turn-based, tactical combat, and as you'd expect in this genre, your position, height, and more matter. You can trigger Sync attacks when you successfully flank enemies, cause foes to Break once you hone in on their weakness and more. Gross says that Beaten Path features over 25 recruitable characters, ten times as many abilities, ten weapon classes with ten times as many weapons, plus a dual-job system. Gross emphasizes party-building as a significant part of the gameplay. Finally, he mentions that "You’ll travel across continents, sail by ship, ride horses, uncover secrets and return to The Haven, a hub where allies gather, conversations change and shops offer new ways to strengthen your party."

Beaten Path will launch on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch in 2027. Wishlist it on Steam if you're interested.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of both IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, as well as our semi-retired interview show, IGN Unfiltered. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

items.title: Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope Gets Welsh Language Dub
items.description: Ahead of the film’s 50th anniversary next year, Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope is being translated into the Welsh language. Titled Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd, the Welsh language dub will be broadcast on S4C and its platforms on December 25, 2026.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Ahead of the film’s 50th anniversary next year, Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope is being translated into the Welsh language.

StarWars.com announced Tuesday that Lucasfilm and Disney are producing the dub of A New Hope with S4C and the Welsh Government via Creative Wales.

Titled Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd, the Welsh language dub will be broadcast on S4C and its platforms on December 25, 2026.

The Welsh dub voice cast includes Osian Morgan as Luke Skywalker, Matthew Rhys (Widow’s Bay) as Han Solo, Rhys Ifans (House of the Dragon) as Obi-Wan Kenobi, Aimee-Ffion Edwards as Princess Leia, Mark Lewis Jones as Darth Vader, Llyr Ifans as C-3PO, Nia Roberts as Aunt Beru, Richard Harrington as Grand Moff Tarkin, The Ring of Power’s Owain Arthur as Red Leader, and Rhodri Meilir as Gold Leader.

Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd is directed by Ellyn Stern and produced by Lucasfilm Director of Distribution Operations Michael Kohn.

“We're really excited about this project for many reasons,” Kohn said in the press release.

“I've been involved in a few Indigenous dubs of Star Wars over the years that aim to preserve and revitalize interest in learning the language. They have been tremendously successful not only in their communities but internationally as well. The chance to celebrate the Welsh language through Star Wars is one we couldn’t pass up.”

For more Star Wars coverage, find out what franchise creator George Lucas thinks of AI and why he believes Hollywood takes the wrong message from focus groups.

items.title: Disney Admits Live-Action Moana and Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu 'Underperformed,' But Says the Movies Still Helped Shift Plenty of Merchandise
items.description: Disney's live-action Moana and Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu both underperformed at the box office, but their ticket sales are only part of the story, the company has argued.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disney's live-action Moana and Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu both underperformed at the box office, but their ticket sales are only part of the story, the company has argued.

As part of its latest financial results, Disney admitted that both Moana and The Mandalorian and Grogu's theatrical revenues had been disappointing, but said that both movies had made up for this to some degree by also shifting plenty of merchandise.

Moana is currently languishing on a $263 million box office, against a $250 million budget, making it almost as bad a box office bomb as the widely-panned live-action Snow White. Factoring in additional marketing costs, the film will not have turned a profit. Sentiment towards the film was not positive ahead of time, with many fans questioning why the project even existed (while others were too busy creating memes featuring The Rock's wig).

The Mandalorian and Grogu, meanwhile, finished its theatrical run on a box office of $345 million against a $165 million budget. While this is a better profit margin than Moana, it is still the lowest box office for any live-action Star Wars film — even Solo. Still, Disney is keen to tell shareholders that ticket sales are only one metric to measure these movies' success.

"These franchise investments contributed to value creation beyond their theatrical releases," Disney said in its financial earnings. In particular, Mandalorian and Grogu "drove healthy growth in retail sales for the Star Wars franchise during the quarter," Disney continued.

"Looking ahead, we expect the live-action Moana to be a strong title on Disney+, building on the success of the original film, which is one of the most streamed movies of all time, and extending the reach of the franchise, which now includes three films, a themed area at EPCOT, and a robust global merchandise business."

Still, despite this positive spin, the chances of a live-action Moana 2 seem slim-to-none. As for the Mandalorian and his young ward, there's no word yet of when or where these characters might appear again. (Upcoming Disney+ series Ahsoka is expected to lay the final pieces of groundwork for an Heir to the Empire project featuring Thrawn, though Dave Filoni's long-promised team-up project currently remains uncertain.)

Elsewhere, Disney celebrated the $1 billion box office success of Toy Story 5, and said that The Devil Wears Prada 2 had also performed well, particularly internationally. Today also marked the announcement of a new initiative to fill Disney+ with user-made TikTok content, which seems to replace the company's earlier plans to flood its streaming platform with AI slop videos made using Sora.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Pokémon Pokopia Version 2.0.0 Released, and Here Are the Full Patch Notes
items.description: Nintendo Switch 2 hit Pokémon Pokopia has received its big Version 2.0.0 update, adding a bunch of free content, support for its Bubbly Basin expansion, and much more.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Nintendo Switch 2 hit Pokémon Pokopia has received its big Version 2.0.0 update, adding a bunch of free content, support for its Bubbly Basin expansion, and much more.

Today's patch is now live on Switch 2 for all Pokémon Pokopia owners, whether you have the game's Expansion Pass or not. As previously announced, all players will get the ability to survive and build underwater for the first time, thanks to the all-new Dive ability. This adds a cute bubble to your Ditto character's head, finally allowing them to survive beneath the waves for more than a few seconds.

All players can now access an array of new recipes, emotes, hair colors, and more, while the patch notes below list out some useful gameplay improvements. As well as changes to make locating Pokémon more straightforward, you'll now be able to perform various actions multiple times in the same interaction, and appraise up to 10 relics at the same time.

Of course, players who own Pokopia's Expansion Pass will also now be able to access its Bubbly Basin DLC. You'll just need to have learnt the new Dive move and upgraded Bleak Beach's Raise the Environment Level quest to level 5. After that, Popplio will appear at the area's Pokémon Center, and guide you to the new Bubbly Basin gate.

Today's full patch notes lie below:

Pokémon Pokopia: Ver. 2.0.0

The following features have been added:

  • Added the move Dive, allowing players to move freely underwater.
  • The Build specialty can now be used to build houses underwater.
  • Added new items such as the portal pod and safe.
    • Recipes can be purchased after increasing Palette Town’s environment level.
  • Added the new pattern, dynamic Ditto print.
    • Can be obtained by talking to Smearguru after acquiring the diploma.
  • Added new emotes: Lie Down and Ready, Set, Go!
    • Can be obtained in Bleak Beach and on Dream Islands.
  • Added five new hair colors: orange, light pink, yellow-green, blue-green, and brown.
  • Added a function to move items in bulk between the storage box and bag.
  • Added a function to delete items placed inside objects such as the garbage bin.
  • Added the ability to fine-tune depth placement when placing windows, doors, and similar items.
  • Added an option in Settings to hide the confirmation message shown when canceling Magnet Rise.
  • Added an option in Settings allowing movement while the move wheel is open.
  • Added motion-sickness reduction settings for the camera.
  • The following items can now be painted: stylish stool, handrail, metal chain, workbench, vending machine, bike, bookcase, Pokémon Center counter, arrow sign, rope.

The following improvements have been implemented:

  • Even if a Pokémon’s habitat is destroyed, it will move back in if the same habitat is rebuilt within a certain area.
  • Pokémon that are sad because furniture was removed will now notice more quickly when the same furniture is replaced.
  • Pokémon that taught you an emote will now respond with the same emote when you use it.
  • If a Pokémon being searched for in the Pokédex is in another town, you can now travel to that town using Return Home.
  • Reduced ordinary conversation indicators so that special Pokémon conversations and requests directed at Ditto stand out more clearly.
  • Lost relics can now be appraised in batches of up to 10 at a time.
  • Paint, Gather Honey, and Collect can now be performed multiple times in the same interaction.
  • During crafting, materials in the storage box next to the workbench will be consumed before materials in the bag.
  • Increased the placement limit for power generators (excluding furnaces) from 64 to 128.
  • Increased the number of different photos that can be displayed in a town from 10 to 40.
  • When sucking up liquid, a short press of the move button to hold liquids in Ditto’s mouth will allow liquid to be held in their mouth without removing it from the environment.
  • When releasing stored water, adjusted water levels now automatically match nearby water levels.
  • Smearguru can now learn patterns from photos stored in References.
  • Improved visibility of the target item when painting with paint balloons.
  • Increased the amount of treasure discoverable with the Dowsing Machine on Dream Islands.
  • Pokémon companions can now follow you while moving with Surf, Glide, Rollout, or Magnet Rise.
  • Inhaling items and opening the bag are now possible while rolling using Rollout.
  • Rollout can now destroy certain natural objects such as large boulders.
  • Surf can now be activated on land by pressing the Surf button while holding the focus button.
  • Improved activation conditions for Surf and Waterfall so they occur more smoothly.
  • Leafage can now be used on farm soil to revert it to a normal soil block.
  • Strength can now be used underwater.
  • Added an All tab to both the Pokédex and Habitat Dex.
  • Made it clearer that buildings can still be remodeled even when items such as the Ditto Flag are attached to roofs or walls.
  • During construction, any Pokémon not assigned to the Build role in a building project can now help with cooking.
  • Prevented treasures in Sparkling Skylands from appearing when using the Dowsing Machine in locations where breaking terrain would cause them to fall.
  • Improved messaging when there are insufficient materials for copying items using the 3D Printer.
  • Items can now be placed on top of square plants.
  • Hide-and-sneak can now be canceled midway.
  • Adjusted in-game event notifications shown at startup so they are displayed only during specific remaining-day periods.
  • Certain roof items now block water.
  • Increased output when crafting curved eaves to 10.
  • Tidal Bell and Clear Bell can now be triggered using laser sensors and switches.
  • Adjusted sound effects for camping chair and sleeping bag.
  • Improved performance for certain rendering processes.

The following issues have been fixed:

  • When talking to a Pokémon that is currently assigned to construct buildings, options such as “Follow me!” may sometimes fail to appear.
  • Suicune and Gholdengo may be unable to travel across water.
  • Pokémon may occasionally fall into the ocean or off cliffs when appearing from their habitats.
  • Even when using honey, Pokémon may sometimes fail to return to their habitats.
  • Using Magnet Rise may occasionally cause Pokémon to scold or warn the player.
  • Pokémon that dislike water may sometimes be unable to move across duckweed and flowering duckweed on the water’s surface.
  • Requests from Pokémon may occasionally ask for items that the requesting Pokémon actually dislikes.
  • When processing berries in the community box, paint may not be produced correctly.
  • The timing of the note played by the music mat (high Do) is offset incorrectly.
  • Certain furniture can be painted through specific procedures even on parts where the colors are not actually changeable.
  • Painting certain items may use more paint than intended.
  • The light color of a painted surface light may fail to change correctly.
  • Under specific conditions, it is possible to place more than one party cooking pot in the same town.
  • Some items may display unnaturally when viewed from a distance.
  • For some items, visual effects may disappear when viewed through glass.
  • Under certain conditions during multiplayer, building may become impossible to complete or cancel.
  • In certain situations, it may be unclear why actions such as building or relocation cannot be performed.
  • On Cloud Islands, players other than the administrator may be able to place a relocation kit.
  • Under certain conditions, a building kit may become unrecoverable when remodeling a house.
  • Under certain conditions, painted portions of the sand house may be reset.
  • Using Rock Smash while falling may cause Ditto’s position or height to become significantly displaced.
  • During the Withered Wasteland request “Clear the path!” Slowpoke may stop moving partway through.
  • During the Sparkling Skylands request “Follow Tinkmaster!” certain actions may prevent the request from progressing.
  • During the Sparkling Skylands request “Pokémon Center tour guide!” searching for Tinkmaster in the Pokédex may guide the player to the town containing their habitat rather than the town where they are currently located.
  • Loading may occasionally fail to finish when returning from a Dream Island.
  • Returning from a Dream Island may incorrectly send the player to Palette Town.
  • Under certain conditions when an online session ends, the player may be transported to a Dream Island.
  • On the Cloud Island loading screen, the player’s gender pronoun may sometimes be displayed incorrectly in some languages.

We have made several additional adjustments and fixed a number of bugs to improve the overall gameplay experience.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Disney+ Announces Plans to Feature User-Made TikTok Content, Just Days After Emmy-Nominated Wonder Man Cancellation
items.description: Disney's streaming service will soon feature user-made content from TikTok, the company has announced.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disney's streaming service will soon feature user-made content from TikTok, the company has announced.

Described as a "first-of-its-kind global deal" that will open doors "for the next generation of creators," the partnership will see Disney-related fan content from TikTok added to Disney+ in the form of "Verts" — short-form vertical videos.

Disney has said it will allow creators access to hundreds of films and series in its back catalogue in return for them pumping out videos that touch on Disney brands, including Star Wars, Marvel, Pixar and shows on FX. The exact guidelines here are unclear, however, and Disney has said it will "thoughtfully curate" the videos it picks to highlight. So, don't expect to see too many Verts criticizing Rise of Skywalker.

In a nutshell, Disney+ gets to add content it has paid next to nothing for, while content creators potentially get their work seen by an enormous audience. It sounds like a great business decision for both sides, though today's announcement will hardly install confidence in the platform's future quality bar — especially just days after the shock cancellation of Emmy-nominated series Wonder Man.

"The best storytellers are fans first," said Asad Ayaz, Chief Marketing and Brand Officer, The Walt Disney Company in a statement. "That has always been true at Disney, and today, fans are celebrating our stories in entirely new ways. This collaboration creates a new bridge between the stories we tell and the creativity they inspire, giving creators a bigger stage to share what they’ve made, and audiences more to discover on Disney+ every day."

Today's announcement comes just months after the abrupt cancellation of Disney's previous push to fill its streaming service with user-made short-form content, via a deal with OpenAI. That partnership would have seen Disney pay $1 billion for the privilege of having 100 of its most beloved characters thrown into OpenAI's Sora video slop engine for users to generate content from. However, the whole thing collapsed after OpenAI ditched Sora, and decided it could make more money elsewhere.

Image credit: Disney

items.title: 'It Seems a Little Open-Ended': Spider-Man: Brand New Day's Jacob Batalon Discusses the Movie's Big Moment Between Peter and Ned
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day actor Jacob Batalon has discussed his interpretation for the movie's big final moment between Peter and Ned.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day actor Jacob Batalon has discussed his interpretation for the movie's big final moment between Peter and Ned.

Warning! Spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day follow...

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter, Batalon was asked about his final scene with Tom Holland, and whether their characters' handshake suggested that Ned's memories of Peter had been restored.

While Batalon stopped short of providing an official confirmation, the actor said that Ned remembering his secret handshake with Peter implied "a slight glint or little glimmer" of recognition had returned.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day picks up the action some five years after Spider-Man: No Way Home, which concluded with Ned, MJ and the rest of the world all forgetting who Spider-Man's real identity was. Years on, Brand New Day confirms that Ned and MJ still don't remember Peter at all, despite the latter finding Peter's letter he wrote to her professing his love.

That said, there are clues that the characters do still remember something of Peter, even subconsciously so. In the scene where Peter hangs out with Ned and MJ in their flat, MJ draws Spider-Man in his Homecoming suit, and at the end of the film, MJ is back on the rooftop she previously visited with Peter, holding the necklace that Peter gave her.

Fans have various theories for what's going on, from Ned and MJ's interactions beginning to unlock their memories naturally, to the effects of Jean Grey's forcefield giving their memories a nudge.

Another clue here seems to come from the Hulk, who said that being possessed by Jean had the effect of unlocking something that had been kept behind a barrier. It's suggested that Hulk also remembers Peter, which is potentially why he lets Spider-Man go and lets himself fall from the building instead.

All of which takes to that handshake with Ned, which Batalon says has been left "a little open-ended."

"What if it’s just muscle memory? What if he just remembers that handshake but nothing else about Peter? What if he just repeats 'Peter' because that’s what Peter says his name is in that moment? I don’t know," Batalon said.

"I feel like it’s really up to interpretation for everyone. There could be a slight glint or little glimmer [of recognition], if you will."

As part of the same interview, Batalon was also asked about Brand New Day's post-credits scene, which features the Spidey Tracker app that Ned built. Unfortunately, Batalon seemed completely in the dark on this. "You think me, of all people, knows top-brass-level information?" he responded. "Come on."

Will MJ and Ned have their memories of Peter fully restored? This is likely something we'll see explored in the inevitable Spider-Man 5, which seems certain now that Brand New Day has done so well at the box office. Indeed, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has noted that there are plans for more Spidey adventures and Holland has said he's keen to help eventually introduce Miles Morales into the MCU.

Image credit: Eric Charbonneau/Sony Pictures via Getty Images

items.title: With Avatar's Future Still Uncertain, James Cameron Now Says He Wants to Prioritize 'Other Stories' For the 'Last Act' of His Career
items.description: Avatar director James Cameron has signaled that he may be ready to move on from the franchise, as the status of its two planned sequels still remains uncertain.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Avatar director James Cameron has signaled that he may be ready to move on from the franchise, as the status of its two planned sequels remains uncertain.

Disney has pencilled in release dates for an Avatar 4 and Avatar 5 over the next five years, but has yet to give the greenlight for production to start. And there are questions over how well these films will perform financially after the waning — but admittedly still enormous — returns for 2025's Avatar: Fire and Ash.

Last year's movie earned $1.4 billion at the box office, a remarkable amount for any film, but around half the money made by the first Avatar ($2.9 billion), and nearly a billion less than Avatar: The Way of Water ($2.3 billion). At the same time, Avatar films are incredibly costly to produce, meaning that they need to earn huge amounts to turn a profit.

With Avatar's future unclear, Cameron has discussed the need to prioritize "other stories" that he wanted to see made during the "last act" of his career. The 71-year-old filmmaker has long had various other ideas for films other than Avatar sequels, though has not directed a non-Avatar blockbuster since 1997's Titanic.

"That's the question of the hour for me," Cameron said in an interview following his receipt of a prestigious Canadian arts award. "There's been momentum in the Avatar universe for 21 years at this point because we started in 2005. I took a little time off to build a submersible and dive to the deepest spot on the planet, as you do, but I came back to Avatar after that. And it's been kind of an unbroken continuum.

"So this is the point where I'm looking at the landscape and asking, 'What are the other stories I want to tell? How many of them do I need to direct myself versus writing and/or producing with other filmmakers?'" he continued.

What are these other stories? Cameron has long discussed adapting Ghosts of Hiroshima, which focuses on the story of a man who survived both bombs that dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in World War 2. Cameron first discussed the project back in 2010 and has continued to show interest, and in 2024 said he hoped he would shoot the film last year (something that did not happen). Other ideas that Cameron has previously discussed include an adaptation of Joe Abercrombie’s dark fantasy book The Devils, plus Terminator and Alita: Battle Angel sequels. Which of these Cameron is considering shooting first, however, remains unclear.

"The criterion — I've literally mapped this out for myself over the last two weeks — I started with, 'What will do the most good?' I put that in block letters at the top," Cameron continued. "And I started looking at all the projects I'm most fond of, asking, 'How's this going to improve our condition? How's that going to make the world better for our kids?'

"I haven't made those decisions yet. I'm still in this liminal state of mapping out... the last act, if you will. And I don't know if that last act will last a year or 20 years."

In April, an update from producer Rae Sanchini stated that the scripts for Avatar 4 and 5 were in hand as the franchise's team continued to move "full speed ahead." But in May, Cameron said he was "looking at some new technologies" to try and get Avatar 4 and 5 made "in half the time for two-thirds of the cost," something that would need to take a year just to figure it out.

Disney has currently scheduled tentative release dates of December 21, 2029 for Avatar 4 and December 19, 2031 for Avatar 5 — but, again, these are just placeholders until plans are made concrete.

Image credit: Photo by Paul Morigi/Getty Images for National Geographic

items.title: Original Grand Tour Hosts Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond, and James May Will Cameo in the New Season
items.description: The original former Top Gear trio set to make appearances alongside their replacements in the returning series.
items.author: Luke Reilly
items.content:
The Grand Tour co-creator Andy Wilman has confirmed that original hosts Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond, and James May will be making cameo appearances in the new season, alongside their replacements. Wilman revealed the plan with 3Bs radio at the Buckingham Literary Festival, via The Independent.

“We’ve got three guys coming soon with a new Grand Tour and we’ve got behind them,” said Wilman. “We’re really supporting them.”

“Our guys are in the shows doing cameos, so we’re wishing them well because we do want to pass that baton on.”

Wilman co-created The Grand Tour with Clarkson, Hammond, and May for Prime Video, and it premiered in late 2016. The show was established after Wilman, Hammond, and May departed the BBC in the wake of Clarkson’s suspension and subsequent sacking from the hugely popular Top Gear. Well over a decade prior, Wilman and Clarkson co-created the revived version of Top Gear that we know today, which debuted in 2002.

The Grand Tour officially revealed its new host line-up back in February, which consists of motoring journalists Thomas Holland and James Engelsman – an existing duo from successful motoring YouTube channel Throttle House – and trainspotting UK social media personality Francis Bourgeois. It was recently confirmed that the new six-episode season will arrive on Prime this September.

While limited to cameos, the involvement of Clarkson, Hammond, and May does position The Grand Tour rather differently to Top Gear, which went through a revolving line-up of hosts after the original trio left – to mixed critic and audience reactions. Top Gear saw eight different hosts from 2016 up until the show was put on ice in 2023.

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

items.title: Joke Game Priced at 200 Dollars Rakes In $1.3 Million on Steam Before Thousands of Players Refund It
items.description: The teenaged developer of a joke game titled This Game Costs 200 Dollars almost made over $1 million before thousands of players refunded it.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The teenaged developer of a joke game titled This Game Costs 200 Dollars almost made over $1 million before thousands of players refunded it.

18-year-old Michael Major is behind the viral game, which is actually a sequel to his previous title, This Game Costs 10 Dollars. Major said he created the game as a simple joke, figuring no one would actually buy it due to its exorbitant price, which is the maximum amount of money that developers can charge on the Steam.

In fact, the Steam page’s ‘About This Game’ section describes it as “the swindle to end all swindles,” with Major writing, “I know some people will buy this game out of sheer curiosity, and I highly recommend you do, too.”

Little did he expect that thousands of players would actually take him up on his offer. As reported by local New Hampshire news outlet WMUR-TV, Major’s simplistic, top-down game raked in $1,345,650… sort of.

As shown by Major’s Steam Works Sales and Activations Report, a total of 6,717 units were sold, with 6,705 of those purchases originating in China. Four were sold within the United States, three in Hong Kong, two in Spain, and one each in Saudi Arabia, Taiwan, and Singapore. Most of these buyers returned the game without even playing it (the average playtime for those who actually did play was around 10 minutes), getting refunds that whittled the impressive $1.3 million figure down to a measly $2,045.

“They might be buying it to return it instantly so they can get some kind of points for the highest amount possible without actually paying $200,” Major speculated, referencing Steam Points, which are rewards that players accrue with each purchase that can be used to snag profile swag and other customization goodies. Steam also allows users to refund any game within 14 days of purchase and less than two hours of total playtime, something these buyers clearly took advantage of.

Major theorized that his prank game could have been used to launder funds, saying, “I’m not joking, I have heard of expensive games on Steam being used for money laundering. I have no idea. I could be on a ‘hit list’ right now.”

Speaking to WMUR-TV, Major joked that he “almost died” when he saw the $1.3 million figure in his Steam Report, saying he would have “quit his job” if he’d actually made that much.

On the opposite end of that spectrum, another indie game developer and Twitch streamer broke down in tears after learning that his tower defense game Tangy TD raked in $31,942 just thirty hours after launch, sparking a viral moment that made the game even more popular.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

This article contains spoilers for Spider-Man: Brand New Day. You've been warned.

A new Spider-Man: Brand New Day fan theory may help explain the ending of the film.

During the climax of Spider-Man: No Way Home, Peter Parker orders Doctor Strange to cast a spell that will make everyone forget about Peter Parker, including his friends and loved ones. It's a powerful moment of self-sacrifice, but one that takes a mental toll on Peter. He's now totally alone; his girlfriend has moved on and has no memory of him, and his best friend has forgotten him.

At the end of Brand New Day, both MJ and Ned appear to be remembering Peter. MJ is seen crying on the rooftop of Midtown High, where the trio would frequently hang out, while also holding on to the necklace Peter gave her. It's not explicitly said, but it seems clear that she is wrestling with her forgotten past in some capacity. However, the more widely-debated scene is the final moment of the film.

Peter reintroduces himself to Ned at a bodega and does their signature handshake, which Ned seems to subconsciously remember. He then exclaims, "Peter!" before it cuts to black. Many viewers believe this signals that the spell is broken for Ned, while others think it's not as cut and dry. However, one TikTok user suggested that there's more magic at play.

@yayaahlyzee he is like part wizard now ?? rewatching the older ones after seeing brand new day and i dont remember that happening . at the end of bnd they do the hand shake , was that enough to give him his memories back ? #spiderman #spidermannowayhome #spidermanbrandnewday #fyp #ned ♬ SPIDER-MAN: Brand New Day - Trailer Music - Ayhan Music

In Spider-Man: No Way Home, Ned and Peter do their handshake after Ned has begun to show signs that he is capable of producing magic using Doctor Strange's sling ring. Later in the film, he conjures portals that introduce the other Spider-Men. Is it possible that the handshake is now charged with magic, and that this, in turn, breaks the spell at the end of Brand New Day? Who's to say! But it's certainly a compelling theory.

In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter, Ned's actor, Jacob Batalon, addressed the ending, but wouldn't confirm or deny any theories or implications it may have.

"First and foremost, does Ned actually remember him, though?" asked Batalon. "It seems a little open-ended. What if it’s just muscle memory? What if he just remembers that handshake but nothing else about Peter? What if he just repeats 'Peter' because that’s what Peter says his name is in that moment? I don’t know. I feel like it’s really up to interpretation for everyone. For me, I think it’s a really cool little nod, so hopefully things happen from there."

He went on to suggest that there might be a "a slight glint or little glimmer" of recognition, though.

It's unclear when we will see the next Spider-Man film with Tom Holland. Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has noted that there are plans for more Spidey adventures and Holland sees a long-term plan that will eventually introduce Miles Morales into the MCU. After Brand New Day shattered box office records, it seems difficult to imagine Sony and Marvel will waste much time, but there's nothing officially on the slate yet.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Reportedly Cut a Scene With a Fan-Favorite Daredevil Character And It Might've Fixed a Plot Hole
items.description: Spider-Man: Brand New Day almost had even more MCU cameos, and one of them may have fixed a slight plot hole.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day spoilers are featured in the article below. You've been warned.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day almost had even more MCU cameos, and one of them may have fixed a slight plot hole.

At the end of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, our beloved wall-crawler jumps in front of a bullet for Jean Grey after The Punisher takes a shot at her. This heroic moment nearly kills him, but he's thankfully rushed to a hospital, with Jean Grey using her powers to keep him alive until doctors stabilize him. However, fans have raised a concern regarding the fact Peter is unmasked in his hospital room, as this would mean there are at least a handful of random people who know his secret identity.

Of course, it's just the nature of the situation, and Peter probably places some trust in the people saving his life. However, there was a cut scene that may have actually helped explain this. According to a post from @JuanEditz on X (who had accurately leaked some details about the film's marketing plans), Claire Temple had a small role in Brand New Day. Rosario Dawson previously confirmed that she reprised her Daredevil role in the film, but didn't reveal the specifics.

there was also another scene cut where the doctors are ripping open his suit but leave his mask on

— juan (@JuanEditzs) August 2, 2026

Now, the X user claims that in a deleted scene, doctors would've cut Peter out of his suit and left his mask on to protect his secret identity. He would've then woken up with his mask still on and then bumped into Claire in the hallway, who was examining an X-Ray. The two would've had a "cute" interaction, and that would've been the end of it. Juan noted that he wasn't sure if Claire was in the room when they cut Spidey's suit off, but speculated that it was certainly possible.

The scene likely would've fixed fan concerns regarding Peter being unmasked by strangers. Claire Temple also likely knows the importance of maintaining a secret identity, since she patched up Daredevil on multiple occasions and has experience with a sensitive matters like this one. As of right now, it's unclear whether Claire will return in a future Marvel project, such as Daredevil: Born Again Season 3.

Nevertheless, none of this actually hurt the movie. Brand New Day just had the biggest domestic opening in history, dethroning Avengers: Endgame. It's also on track to score over $2 billion at the box office and is among some of the best-reviewed Marvel films in history.
